svg.title: moe-service-handler data flow: experts split across the workers
svg.desc: Start · The controller loads its own weights from its SSD: embedding, attention, router, head. Start · It reads every expert from the SSD and sends each worker the half it owns. Start · Each worker keeps all its experts in RAM (8.44 GiB at 4-bit): ready to serve. 1 · The prompt comes in to the controller. 2 · Layer 1: the controller runs attention and the router, which picks 8 of 256 experts. 3 · It sends the hidden state to both workers at once, each with the picked experts it owns. 4 · Both workers compute their experts at the same time. 5 · Both send their expert outputs back. 6 · The controller adds them up: layer 1 is done. 7 · Steps 2–6 repeat for layers 2 to 40: about 40 round trips per token. 8 · After layer 40, the controller's head picks the token. 9 · The controller streams the token to the client; the next token goes back to step 2. Now and then · rebalance: one expert is read from the SSD and moved to the less busy worker.
svg.text: split = "experts" · built on the mock engine; the real engine waits for streammoe · docs/expert-parallel.md
The experts are split across the workers, so the controller sends each layer to both at once.
Start · The controller loads its own weights from its SSD: embedding, attention, router, head
Start · It reads every expert from the SSD and sends each worker the half it owns
Start · Each worker keeps all its experts in RAM (8.44 GiB at 4-bit): ready to serve
1 · The prompt comes in to the controller
2 · Layer 1: the controller runs attention and the router, which picks 8 of 256 experts
3 · It sends the hidden state to both workers at once, each with the picked experts it owns
4 · Both workers compute their experts at the same time
5 · Both send their expert outputs back
6 · The controller adds them up: layer 1 is done
7 · Steps 2–6 repeat for layers 2 to 40: about 40 round trips per token
8 · After layer 40, the controller's head picks the token
9 · The controller streams the token to the client; the next token goes back to step 2
Now and then · rebalance: one expert is read from the SSD and moved to the less busy worker

Network: per layer ~8 KiB out and ~32 KiB back per worker; ~40 round trips per token ≈ 2–8 ms (estimate, not measured).
Unified memory: on Apple silicon RAM and GPU memory are the same. The math runs on the GPU; the CPU runs network, scheduler, HTTP.
Experts load once at start from the controller's SSD; each has one home worker, rebalanced by use. Short of memory, a worker frees cold ones.
